events.title: The confirmation of the Council of Trent
events.shortBlurb: Pope Pius IV confirmed the decrees of the Council of Trent, sealing the reform that would shape Catholic life for four centuries…
body: On 26 January 1564 Pope Pius IV confirmed the decrees of the Council of Trent with the bull Benedictus Deus, reserving their authoritative interpretation to the Apostolic See. The council, the nineteenth ecumenical council of the Church, had met in twenty-five sessions between 13 December 1545 and 4 December 1563, under Popes Paul III, Julius III, and Pius IV, to answer the Protestant Reformation and reform the Church from within.

Its decrees settled Catholic teaching on Scripture and tradition, original sin, justification, the sacraments, the Mass, and the veneration of saints, while its reform canons commanded bishops to reside in their dioceses and ordered that priests be trained in seminaries. Some 255 fathers subscribed the final decrees, and Pius IV established a congregation of cardinals to guard their execution.

The popes who followed carried the council's work into practice: the Roman Catechism of 1566, the revised Breviary of 1568, and the Roman Missal of 1570 under Pius V. The Tridentine settlement governed Catholic worship and discipline for four hundred years, until the Second Vatican Council.
